back: Channels that communicate information, ideas and entertainment to many people at once: print, electronic and social media.
A fixed, oversimplified idea about a group of people, e.g. that only men can be engineers.
The ability to find, understand, question and judge media messages, and to share content responsibly.
Misinformation: false content shared in error. Disinformation: false content spread on purpose to deceive.

front: Name the three groups of media with an example of each.
back: Print (newspaper), electronic/broadcast (radio, television), social/digital (social networking site).

front: Name five roles of the media in socialisation.
back: Informing, educating, entertaining, providing role models, spreading values, advertising, shaping opinions.

front: Four questions to ask before sharing a message?
back: Who made it? When? Where else is it reported? Why was it made?

front: Why is radio important in rural areas?
back: It reaches remote places in local languages, needs no reading skills and can run on batteries.

front: Give three disadvantages of the media as a socialising agent.
back: False information, harmful (violent or explicit) content, stereotypes, foreign values, wasteful advertising.
